commit_subject: Fix Louisiana resident core review findings
description: Independent review found four initial issues: unqualified aggregate names, spouse items applied outside joint returns, incorrect retrofit operator ordering/unpinned regulatory eligibility, and filing-status fallback.

decisive_quotes.quote: "Individual" means a natural person. However, for any taxable year, a husband and wife may file a joint income tax return
Six thousand dollars of annual disability income received by an individual shall be exempt from state income taxation.

provision_review.why: provision.txt (47:32) only states the 3% rate and says nothing about spouse amounts, exemptions or filing status. 47:44.1(B) grants the exemption per individual, and 47:293(6) makes an individual a single natural person, with a husband and wife combined only on a joint return. So a spouse's exemption, active-duty exclusion or volunteer deduction can appear only on a joint return. The pre-fix module adds them for single, head-of-household and married-separate returns too.

triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: The pre-fix module added the spouse's disability-income exemption, active-duty-outside-Louisiana exclusion, and volunteer deduction for any taxpayer regardless of filing status, so a single, head-of-household, or married-filing-separately return picked up spouse-level amounts that only exist on a joint return (and, separately, it computed the 47:293 retrofit amount as fifty percent of cost minus incentives and fell back to the single/separate standard deduction when no recognized status was selected).
triage.triage_notes: Single-module commit with three distinct fidelity defects fixed at once, plus a scope-honesty renaming pass; I labeled the kind by the broadest-footprint defect. (1) wrong_entity_or_scope: three spouse branches gained 'la_2026_resident_filing_status_joint and ...' guards. (2) amount_mismatch: retrofit formula changed from rate * max(0, cost - incentives) to max(0, rate*max(0,cost) - max(0,incentives)); I read us-la/statute/47:293 through the pinned corpus release and it reads 'an amount equal to fifty percent of the cost paid or incurred ... less the value of any municipally sponsored, state-sponsored, or federally sponsored financial incentives', i.e. the incentive offset applies after the fifty percent, so the pre-fix ordering overstated the deduction whenever incentives were nonzero; the commit also adds a second proof atom quoting that 'less the value of...' clause. (3) polarity_or_logic: the pre-fix standard deduction had a fail-open else-branch returning the single/separate amount for any unrecognized or empty filing status; the fix adds selection_count/selection_valid rules and returns 0 (and zero partial tax-table income) unless exactly one status is set. The renames (positive_exempt_income -> encoded_positive_exempt_income, tax_table_income -> partial_tax_table_income_before_held_adjustments, etc.) plus the new deferred_outputs entries are scope-labeling/claim-narrowing, not meaning changes by themselves; but dropping the retrofit amount out of la_2026_resident_encoded_direct_deductions_before_held_adjustments does change the aggregate, and the retrofit rule also lost its 'if la_2026_resident_qualifying_retrofit_completed_in_tax_year' gate (which is itself grounded in 47:293(2)(b) 'claimed on the return for the taxable year in which the work is completed') because the rule is now nominal-only and excluded from aggregates - a reviewer may want to flag that as a coverage loss rather than a gain. Follow-up commits in the same PR: 8d3d0f5e3 'Fail closed Louisiana spouse components' (re-review found the spouse branches needed valid-status AND joint, not just joint) and bee5412e8 'Fix Louisiana EITC rate validation'. No PR reviews or review comments were captured in the bundle; the commit body is empty, so the quote comes from the PR body.
triage.verifier_justification: The anchored rule's formula changed meaning exactly as described: each spouse-level branch in la_2026_resident_disability_income_exemption, la_2026_resident_active_duty_outside_louisiana_exclusion, and la_2026_resident_volunteer_deduction gained an `la_2026_resident_filing_status_joint and ...` conjunct, narrowing the population from any return to joint returns only. The companion fixture proves the pre-fix behavior was live and wrong, not defensive: the old case `disability_and_active_duty_caps_apply_per_spouse_at_and_above_boundary` set `filing_status_single: true` with spouse flags true and expected `disability_income_exemption: 12000` / `active_duty_outside_louisiana_exclusion: 100000`, and it was rewritten to `married_separate_ignores_spouse_disability_active_duty_and_volunteer_amounts` expecting 6000 / 50000 / volunteer 0. The pinned source supports the narrowing: 47:44.1(B) exempts disability income "received by an individual," and 47:293(6) defines "Individual" as a natural person who reaches the return only via the joint-return option ("a husband and wife may file a joint income tax return"), so a single/HOH/MFS return cannot carry a spouse's individual amount. Filing status and household member set are precisely wrong_entity_or_scope, and no other listed kind fits the anchored formula change better.
triage.verifier_notes:
Refutation attempts that failed: (1) "the gate is defensive, spouse inputs would be zero anyway" — refuted by the rewritten fixture, which had a single filer receiving 12000/100000 pre-fix; spouse flags are raw undeclared inputs with no zeroing rule in the module. (2) "renames only" — refuted; the renames (positive_exempt_income -> encoded_positive_exempt_income, tax_table_income -> partial_..._before_held_adjustments) are mechanical, but they sit alongside three formula changes with changed fixture values. (3) "new coverage never claimed" — refuted; the module claimed a filing-status-aware resident core and mis-scoped spouse items within it.

Reviewer caveats worth carrying: this commit bundles at least two ADDITIONAL, distinct fidelity defects that are not wrong_entity_or_scope, and if the corpus wants one kind per item they should probably be split out. (a) amount_mismatch in the retrofit rule: `la_2026_retrofit_deduction_rate * max(0, cost - incentives)` became `max(0, rate * max(0, cost) - max(0, incentives))`; the added proof atom excerpt is "less the value of any municipally sponsored, state-sponsored, or federally sponsored financial incentives for the retrofitting cost paid", and 47:293(2)(a)(i) reads "an amount equal to fifty percent of the cost paid or incurred" — the new fixture `retrofit_incentive_is_subtracted_after_half_of_cost_before_cap` gives 3000 where the old ordering gave 4000 (cost 10000, incentives 2000). (b) polarity_or_logic in la_2026_resident_standard_deduction: the old `else` fell open to `la_2026_standard_deduction_single_or_separate` when no status was selected; it now returns 0 unless la_2026_resident_filing_status_selection_valid holds (new fixtures all_filing_statuses_false_fails_closed and conflicting_filing_statuses_fail_closed, plus two existing fixtures that had to flip `filing_status_single: false` -> `true` to keep their old outputs). The retrofit change also dropped the `la_2026_resident_qualifying_retrofit_completed_in_tax_year` input branch and removed retrofit from the aggregate because LAC 61:I.1937 is absent from the pinned corpus — that piece reads as untraceable_branch / deferral rather than wrong scope.

Provenance caveat: f1ed255931 is a pre-merge review-fix commit inside PR #1026, the PR that ADDS this module (merged 2026-07-23). The defect was caught in review and never existed in a released module. It is still a real encoding defect with a real formula correction, but if the corpus is meant to hold post-release regressions only, this item is in scope by accident.
